newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Trgovacka posts HRK27.8 mln net profit.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Trgovacka posts HRK27.8 mln net profit.

text.p: Croatian private bank Trgovacka Banka said on Monday it made 27.8 million kuna net profit in the year to December 31, compared to 23.0 million in 1995.

The bank will use 9.4 million to pay a dividend of 220 kuna per share. There will be no new share issue but it plans to increase the nominal value of the shares to 1,100 kuna from a current 1,059.70 kuna, it said in a statement.
Trgovacka said it would use some 1.4 million kuna to boost cash reserves and 2.6 million to increase its base capital.
In the statement, announcing the annual shareholders' meeting for June 19, the bank said it would retain some 14.3 million kuna.

Its 1996 pre-tax profit rose to 36.4 million kuna from 30.3 million in 1995. Total income grew to 71 million kuna from 56 million the previous year, but costs also increased, to 34.8 million from 24 million.
The bank said earlier it was seeking to increase its share of the fragmented Croatian market to around five percent.
Trgovacka was one of the smaller banks in Croatia to get a credit line of 10 million marks last year from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
